boy1: Neck pain after an accident or a fall? How long does whiplash last, should you wear a neck collar, and when should you see a doctor? Warning signs and six exercises to do at home.
boy3: Was your head suddenly jolted forwards and backwards in a road accident, a fall or while playing sport? This kind of neck injury is called whiplash. It usually gets better within 2–3 months. Staying active, rather than wearing a neck collar, is the most important part of recovery.

boy16: A sudden movement of the head forwards, backwards or sideways strains the tissues of the neck.
boy17: The most common causes are road accidents, slips and falls, and sports injuries.
boy18: Carry on with your everyday activities. It may hurt a little, but it speeds up recovery. Don’t rest your neck for long periods; change position often.

boy42: No. The NHS says a neck collar does not help recovery, and an NHS physiotherapy leaflet states that research shows a collar delays recovery. You are advised to carry on with your everyday activities rather than resting your neck for long periods.
boy43: Whiplash usually gets better within 2–3 months, but some people have symptoms for longer. If there is no improvement within a week, or you have not returned to most of your normal activities within 6 weeks, you can see your doctor.
boy45: Most people recover with simple advice and by staying active. In a large UK trial of 599 people with persisting symptoms, up to six physiotherapy sessions led to slightly faster recovery at 4 months than a single advice session; there was no difference at 8 and 12 months. If your symptoms are not settling, a personalised assessment can help guide you.
